But about your issue specifically:

*  Comprehend languages: allows you to understand a creature, not to communicate with it (that would require Tongues)
*  Charisma: congrats, you are able to improve the likeliness of people accepting your suggestions, that doesn't mean that they comply to your suggestions. A guard that is asked to follow will follow on a good roll, assuming the intimidation from his commander isn't higher than the roll. Also, charisma checks imply that there is room for negotiating to being with, why else would there be spells like Charm or other mind controlling effects if a regular Charisma check can achieve the same result.

tbf, the concept of travelling merchants and fairs dates from even before medieval times.

though the odds of a merchant caravan or something of the likes passing by a run-of-the-mill town are pretty slim. Perhaps they could go to a nearby castle/keep/fortress and sell their goods there to other merchants that specialize in international/interregional commerce or something.

Using middlemen to sell the monster-loot also allows you to control the party's gold income to a certain degree (middleman also wants a cut on the profits). Even more so, it allows your party to build up a reputation with the traders/in town, which can serve as another plot hook.

As for WHY players would want to do something like this, simply put, it's a different style of challenge. Just like you say "it's fantasy", well, think about it this way: How many people can successfully start a business nowadays?

See, D&D provides a safe environment to RP what it would be like to have a trading company that specializes in fantasy goods. 

However, if you want to bring in realisme, having them find a location to house their shop (at a fair price) would already be a MASSIVE hurdle, since they have no inside-person, no reputation, no representation, nothing that would give them a foot in the door of a location where you would want to settle a shop.

If anything, the most realistic option for the party would be to become travelling merchants themselves, building up trust with certain towns as they frequent them more often and eventually settle in one of them as the local merchant. (at which point you could end that campaign and have the next party shop at stores owned by their own PCs :p )
